title: Research
text:
Programmable photonic circuits offer a scalable hardware platform for AI computing with light. I design silicon nitride (SiN) photonic integrated circuits, from device modeling and simulation to layout, foundry tape-out, and optical measurement.

A nonlinear unitary optical device that combines a Mach-Zehnder interferometer with resonator-coupled waveguides, providing power-preserving nonlinearity for optical neural networks.
A review of programmable photonic unitary circuits and their fidelity–scalability trade-offs for light computing.

title: Research
text:
Optical Inverse Design

Designing large-scale optical materials is limited by the cost of computing how light scatters. I develop inverse-design methods that describe wave scattering with graphs and hypergraphs, enabling fast design of disordered optical materials with targeted scattering.

Hypergraph compression of wave scattering designs large-scale materials with \(O(N^{1/L})\) time complexity, breaking the conventional \(O(N)\) limit.
Correlated gain and loss extend hyperuniformity and stealthiness to non-Hermitian materials, enabling directional control of scattering.

title: Research
text:
Topological Photonics

Topological photonics protects light against fabrication imperfections and experimental perturbations. I develop SiN photonic devices that exploit non-Abelian topology for robust and programmable control of light.

Non-Abelian braiding devices, designed with coupled-mode theory, verified by FDTD simulation, and experimentally characterized after fabrication.
Topological unitary circuits, now in fabrication through a Ligentec foundry run.


Manuscripts in preparation

title: Research
text:
Quantum Photonics

Photonic quantum technologies rely on indistinguishable photons and precisely aligned optics. I lead a five-member quantum optics team in our lab, building photon-pair experiments and automating how they are tuned.

Hong–Ou–Mandel interference of photon pairs from spontaneous parametric down-conversion, measured by time-correlated coincidence counting.
Reinforcement-learning control of mirror alignment and path delay that maximizes interference visibility without manual tuning.
